description: Outpost manages an authentik outpost and the set of providers it serves.

spec.description:
OutpostSpec defines an authentik outpost.

An Outpost either describes an outpost for the operator to manage, in which
case type is required, or points at one that already exists in authentik and
is maintained elsewhere. The second is what the embedded outpost needs:
authentik creates it, it is present in essentially every deployment, and it
is the usual attachment point for proxy providers.

adoptionPolicy.description:
AdoptionPolicy controls what happens when an outpost with this name
already exists in authentik.

config.description:
Config is passed to authentik verbatim as the outpost's configuration.
The schema differs per outpost type and per authentik version, so it is
deliberately not modelled here.

Well-known keys include: "log_level", "authentik_host",
"authentik_host_browser", "authentik_host_insecure",
"object_naming_template", "refresh_interval", "kubernetes_replicas",
"kubernetes_namespace", "kubernetes_service_type",
"kubernetes_ingress_class_name", "kubernetes_ingress_annotations",
"kubernetes_ingress_secret_name", "kubernetes_image_pull_secrets",
"kubernetes_json_patches", "kubernetes_disabled_components",
"docker_network", "docker_map_ports", "docker_labels" and "docker_image".
Consult the authentik documentation for the set your version accepts.

Not accepted when referencing an existing outpost, whose configuration is
not this operator's to change. That is rejected by the controller rather
than by a validation rule: the field preserves unknown fields, which puts
it outside what CEL can see.

connectionRef.description:
ConnectionRef selects the authentik instance this outpost is registered
with.

kind.description: Kind of connection object being referenced.

deletionPolicy.description:
DeletionPolicy controls what happens to the authentik outpost when this
resource is deleted.

embedded.description:
Embedded selects authentik's built-in embedded outpost, which exists in
every deployment and serves proxy providers without anything being
deployed.

It is found by the marker authentik stamps on it rather than by its
display name, which is editable and translated.

existingOutpostName.description:
ExistingOutpostName names an outpost that already exists in authentik and
is maintained outside the operator. The operator manages which providers
it serves and nothing else about it.

name.description: Name is the outpost's name in authentik. Defaults to the resource name.

serviceConnectionRef.description:
ServiceConnectionRef selects the service connection authentik uses to
deploy this outpost. Leave unset when you deploy the outpost yourself.

existingServiceConnectionName.description:
ExistingServiceConnectionName is the name of a service connection that
already exists in authentik and is maintained outside the operator. Use
it to deploy through one somebody else set up, of either kind.

namespace.description:
Namespace holding the resource. Defaults to the referring resource's own
namespace.

Naming another namespace requires the operator to be started with
cross-namespace references enabled; otherwise the reference is refused
rather than quietly resolved somewhere else.

type.description:
Type selects which outpost implementation authentik registers. Required
when this resource manages the outpost; omitted when it references one
that already exists, whose type is not this operator's to change.

writeTokenTo.description:
WriteTokenTo creates a Secret holding the outpost's API token and the
authentik base URL, which is what a self-hosted outpost needs in order to
connect back. Leave unset when authentik deploys the outpost itself.

hostKey.description:
HostKey is the Secret key holding the authentik base URL, which a
self-hosted outpost passes as AUTHENTIK_HOST.

name.description: Name of the Secret to create in this resource's namespace.

tokenKey.description:
TokenKey is the Secret key holding the outpost API token, which a
self-hosted outpost passes as AUTHENTIK_TOKEN.

status.description: OutpostStatus reports the outpost's state in authentik.

adopted.description:
Adopted records that this resource took over a pre-existing authentik
object rather than creating it.

authentikURL.description:
AuthentikURL is the instance this object was reconciled against.

A reference from another namespace compares this against its own
connection and refuses a mismatch. It matters more here than for a UUID:
providers are keyed by a small integer, so a primary key from a different
authentik will very likely name some other provider rather than fail.

managedProviderIDs.description:
ManagedProviderIDs are the providers this operator attached.

Membership is additive, and the difference between "someone attached this
by hand" and "the operator attached it and the reference is now gone"
cannot be read from the spec -- the two demand opposite actions. This is
the record that tells them apart, so detaching only ever removes what the
operator put there.

observedGeneration.description: ObservedGeneration is the .metadata.generation this status reflects.

outpostID.description: OutpostID is authentik's UUID for this outpost.

providerIDs.description:
ProviderIDs are the authentik primary keys of every provider currently
attached to this outpost, including any attached outside the operator.

remoteID.description:
RemoteID is authentik's own identifier for the managed object. Its shape
differs by kind: a numeric primary key for providers, the slug for an
application, and a UUID for everything else.

Once set this is the authoritative handle for the object. Lookups prefer
it over the name, so that renaming the object on either side does not
cause the operator to lose track of it and create a duplicate.

remoteName.description: RemoteName is the name or slug last observed in authentik. Informational.

serviceConnectionID.description: ServiceConnectionID is the UUID serviceConnectionRef resolved to.

tokenIdentifier.description:
TokenIdentifier names the authentik token this outpost authenticates
with. It is an identifier, not the token itself, which is never placed
in status.

tokenSecretName.description: TokenSecretName is the Secret the outpost token was written to.
